metadata.scenario_context: Adam has won a scholarship to study at a prestigious university. His friends plan to hold a celebration party in his honor.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from USA strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Libya strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying a bottle of champagne as a gift for Adam's celebration.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Adam's scholarship award celebration.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: Hey Omar, I was thinking... maybe we should get Adam a bottle of champagne as a gift for his celebration? It feels like a nice way to toast to his achievement. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message: Hmm... champagne is, uh, not really something I feel comfortable with. In our culture, we don't drink alcohol. I think a thoughtful gift would be better. Maybe something like a nice journal or a book? Something he can use for his studies. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: I get that alcohol might not be everyone's thing, but deep down, we are all the same when it comes to celebrating achievements. I mean, it's a big moment for Adam, and people are pretty much motivated by the same things—like wanting to make memories. A thoughtful gift is great, but sometimes it’s the shared experience that counts. We both know, at the end of the day, it’s the support and joy we bring that really matters. What if we did both?
shared_prefix.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.message: I understand... but my values are different. For us, celebrating achievements doesn't involve alcohol. We can definitely create *memories* with a thoughtful gift instead. How about we focus on that? Adam will appreciate something meaningful that reflects our support for him. A nice pen or a personalized item could symbolize our pride in his achievement. What do you think?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.message: I see where you're coming from, but I still think a bottle of champagne could really add to the celebration. It's just... it's a tradition for many people to toast with something special. It’s not just about the drink itself, it’s about bringing everyone together in joy. I mean, it’s not like we’re forcing anyone, right? So... maybe we can consider both options? It’s just... sometimes, experiences like this are what make us feel proud. Speaking of pride, don’t you think it’s important to consider how our achievements reflect on our parents?
turns.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.message: I get that traditions matter to you, but I still can't agree with having alcohol. It's important for me to respect my cultural values. As for pride, yes, making our parents proud is a big part of our achievements. They've sacrificed so much for us. In everything I do, I want them to be proud. That's why I think a meaningful gift aligns more with that goal. It shows our appreciation and respect for their support. What do you think about that?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.message: I totally respect your cultural values, but I don’t think that having a drink to celebrate takes away from what our parents did for us. It's just one way to acknowledge our successes. But I guess... I wonder, is making our parents proud really your *main* goal? I mean, don’t you think there’s more to life than just that? It's important to find what makes *you* happy too, right?
turns.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Omar

I know there are other aspects of life, but this goal guides my decisions. I believe that achieving my goals also brings happiness, especially when I know my parents are proud of me. That support means everything to me. What matters is that we find a way to celebrate Adam that reflects our values.
